summary:
The Cochrane review is by Flemming and Cullum, "Laser therapy for venous leg ulcers" (CD001182). Its earlier 2000 version found no evidence of any benefit associated with low level laser therapy on venous leg ulcer healing. The 2014 update (CD001182.pub2) is listed in the same record. One trial in that review reported a difference: significantly more ulcers completely healed in the group receiving a combination of laser and infrared light compared with non-coherent, unpolarised red light. The review's authors called this one small study and said more research is needed.

The search did not return the full 2014 text, so I can't confirm its final conclusions. The record also shows a "WITHDRAWN" label near the 2000 entry, and I couldn't tell from these results what that refers to. Check the Cochrane Library directly for the current status and conclusions of CD001182.pub2.

Other results were individual trials, not the Cochrane review. A 2005 randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 685-nm therapy found no statistically significant differences in reduction of wound size between the three groups.
